title: Counting or Not Counting: Jordan's Rookie Ledger Has Exactly One Win on It
body: Every club history starts somewhere, and Jordan's starts in 2026, when the Buckaroo Football League expanded to eight teams and handed him the keys to Counting or not Counting GV. He arrived as a numbers guy in a league full of football guys, which is a bold strategy when the scoreboard is the only number anyone checks. Seven weeks in, the spreadsheet reads 1-6 with 622.5 points for, roughly 89 a week, and title odds that have been rounded all the way down to 0%.

The high point came in week 5, when JMoney dropped a season-best 119.7 on Zoe. It remains his only win, which means his lone victory came against his own fiancée, and the scouting report suggests Zoe will not be forgetting it. The low point came two weeks later: a 60.9-point week 7 against Ramon, the kind of output that makes a marching band halftime show look like a high-scoring affair.

The head-to-head page is short and brutal. Jordan is 0-1 against Randy, Sonny, Alan, Mekhi, Kaushal and Ramon, and 1-0 against Zoe, so for now his only rivalry is the one he'll be hearing about at home. Everyone else in the league has one clean entry in their ledger against him, and the challenge for the rest of his career is turning those zeroes into something worth counting.

As a manager, Jordan has not been passive about the slide. He's made 7 pickups and swung 1 trade, a rookie willing to work the waiver wire rather than ride out a 1-6 start quietly. The playoff record sits at 0-0, there's no Buckaroo Bowl banner and no last-place finish yet, and the season is still in progress. The math says this year is over; the profile says Jordan's story in this league has barely started.
